subject: Re: DPA Clarifications — Summit Bank (PII, Retention, Subprocessors)
messages:
From: Daniel Reyes <daniel.reyes@summitbank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Amira Khan <amira.khan@summitbank.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up — DPA questions from today's call

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the call today — helpful overview of Redwood's hosting and private deployment options. A couple of follow-ups for our legal/privacy team so we can progress procurement:

1) Controller vs. Processor: Please confirm how Redwood defines the relationship in the standard DPA for Summit Bank. Our counsel needs to know whether Redwood is a processor acting under Summit's instructions or if any joint-controller obligations exist for model outputs/feature engineering.

2) Subprocessors: Can you provide a current list of subprocessors (cloud providers, telemetry vendors, audit/logging providers)? We need company names and the categories of processing they perform.

3) Breach notice SLA: What is Redwood's contractual breach notification timeframe (e.g., within 72 hours)? Also what is your typical incident investigation / root-cause timeline?

4) Data retention: For PII and system logs (access logs, request/response logs, KV cache), what retention windows are configurable? Is there a default? Can we set retention per-environment?

We'd like a DPA redline to review. Can you loop in legal if needed? I'll also share this thread with our procurement contact.

Thanks,
Daniel Reyes
Senior Procurement Manager
Summit Bank

[Attachment: call-notes-20260814.txt]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Reyes <daniel.reyes@summitbank.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up — DPA questions from today's call

Hi Daniel — great speaking with you as well. Appreciate the clear list. High-level answers below and next steps at the bottom. I've attached our latest DPA redline (v1) and the security questionnaire we discussed.

1) Controller/Processor: In our standard DPA Redwood is the processor for customer content — we process on behalf of the customer and do not assert independent control over customer-provided data. We include language acknowledging that customers control any PII they submit. If there are specific data flows (e.g., joint modeling/feedback loops) that Summit expects to be treated differently, please flag and we can have legal review.

2) Subprocessors: We'll include a current subprocessor list in the DPA redline appendix. High-level: public cloud providers (AWS/GCP/Azure) for hosted infra; analytics/telemetry vendors for operational metrics; object storage providers for backups (where applicable). Rishi will send the canonical list and categories.

3) Breach notice: Our standard commitment is to notify customers of security incidents without undue delay and provide an initial notification within 72 hours for incidents affecting customer-controlled data, consistent with common standards. Rishi & Ethan can confirm operational timelines for investigation and remediation.

4) Data retention: By default, request/response logs and KV caches are retained for 30 days in hosted mode; customers can request reduced retention or enable longer retention via configuration on Dedicated/Private deployments. For Private deployments Summit would control retention entirely. We can include explicit per-environment retention options in the DPA.

Next steps:
- Attached: Summit-Bank_DPA_Redline_v1.pdf and Summit_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx (please review).
- Rishi: I'll hand off subprocessor and breach-notice SLA specifics to you and Ethan for legal/ops detail.
- Can we schedule a 30-minute legal call early next week to walk through the DPA redline? Daniel — what times look good for your counsel?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Daniel Reyes <daniel.reyes@summitbank.com>

Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up — DPA questions from today's call

Marissa — thanks for the quick reply and the attachments. A couple of clarifying items before we loop legal:

- The "processor" designation is good. We just need to be explicit in the DPA around outputs: if Redwood stores derived model outputs or uses aggregated non-PII telemetry for model improvement, is Summit considered controller for those outputs or does Redwood retain any rights? Please confirm the standard clause.

- Subprocessor list: can Rishi confirm whether any third parties access raw request/response content for debugging or model tuning? We need to know if any subprocessors can see PII under normal operations or only under exceptional/controlled circumstances.

- Breach notice: 72 hours initial notification is acceptable. For contract redlines, would Redwood accept language committing to 72-hour initial notice and updates as investigation progresses?

- Retention: For hosted demo/testing we need retention <7 days for session logs. Is that configurable now or would that require a product change?

If you can get Rishi & Ethan to confirm those bullet points, we'll share with our counsel and propose times for a call.

Best,
Daniel

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Reyes <daniel.reyes@summitbank.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up — DPA questions from today's call

Hi Daniel — thanks, answers below (and I copied our legal/ops owners for any additional nuance).

- Model outputs/rights: Our standard DPA states that customers retain rights to their data and derived outputs. Redwood may use aggregated, de-identified telemetry to improve service quality, but we do not use customer content (including derived outputs that can be linked back to a customer) to train models unless explicitly authorized in writing. We'll add an explicit clause in the next redline indicating no training on customer-content-derived outputs without consent.

- Subprocessors & access to content: Rishi: short answer — subprocessors do not access customer raw content under normal production operations. Access to raw request/response data is restricted to a small set of authorized SRE/ops engineers and is audited; access for debugging/model tuning is performed under strict controls and, where required, under NDA and documented exceptions. I'll ask Rishi to provide the current canonical subprocessor list and a brief access policy statement.

- Breach notice: We can accept the 72-hour initial notice language and commit to iterative updates as the investigation progresses. We'll reflect that in the DPA redline.

- Retention: For hosted/demo environments we can enable a <7-day retention policy for logs as a configuration in our system — it is not the default, but we can set it per-customer for hosted trials. For Dedicated/Private, you control retention policy. I'll note this explicitly in the redline and have ops document the configuration steps.

Next steps (concrete):
1) Rishi & Ethan to produce: a) canonical subprocessor list with categories, b) access policy for raw content, c) confirmation of 72-hour notification + iterative updates.
2) I'll produce DPA_Redline_v2 with the wording changes above and share a DocuSign link for convenience.
3) Proposed 30-min call: Tue 8/18 10:00am PT or Wed 8/19 9:00am PT — please let me know which works for your counsel.
